items.title: Critical thinking dispositions and perceived support-dependence discrepancy in GenAI-assisted learning: evidence from human–AI interaction pathways
items.abstract: Background Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can support academic performance while also creating a perceived gap between AI-supported task completion and independently available competence. This study examined how multidimensional critical thinking dispositions are associated with cognitive offloading, cognitive enhancement, and perceived support-dependence discrepancy (PSD) in GenAI-assisted learning. Methods A cross-sectional survey was administered through Wenjuanxing from March 15 to May 20, 2026, using stratified purposive sampling across six Chinese universities. Of 990 submitted questionnaires, 797 eligible and complete responses were retained. The hypothesized pathways were tested using structural equation modeling, with a separate observed-score moderation analysis for academic stress and additional robustness and measurement-model assessments. Results Inquisitiveness was positively associated with cognitive enhancement (β = 0.515, p < 0.001) and cognitive offloading (β = 0.270, p < 0.001). Open-mindedness (β = 0.091, p = 0.039) and systematicity (β = 0.096, p = 0.029) showed small positive associations with cognitive enhancement, whereas analyticity and truth-seeking were not significantly associated with either interaction pathway. Cognitive offloading (β = 0.448, p < 0.001) and cognitive enhancement (β = 0.207, p < 0.001) were positively associated with PSD. The Academic Stress × Cognitive Offloading interaction was not significant (β = 0.048, p = 0.123; delta R-squared = 0.002). Alternative CFA specifications, a common-method-factor analysis, and reliability sensitivity analyses yielded broadly consistent focal conclusions, while the HTMT assessment provided qualified evidence of discriminant validity. Conclusion Critical thinking dispositions showed heterogeneous associations with GenAI interaction pathways, and both offloading and enhancement were associated with perceived support-dependent competence gaps. Because the outcome was measured with a single self-report item and the design was cross-sectional, the findings indicate statistical associations rather than objectively verified overconfidence, calibration bias, or causal effects.

items.title: Cross-Domain Knowledge Retrieval Framework for Power Dispatching Based on Large Language Models and Hybrid Vector-Relational Databases
items.abstract: The paper introduces a new Cross-Domain Knowledge Retrieval Framework that is aimed at optimizing dispatching of power in the current electricity grids. The framework combines Large Language Models (LLMs) with hybrid vectors-relational databases to use structured and unstructured data to make better decisions. Conventional grid management systems usually operate with limited datasets and invariable models and this may lead to inefficient power generation, high operation cost and poor grid stability. Conversely, the proposed system works with various sources of data, such as live grid load data, energy prices, and weather projections to provide adaptable and cost-efficient solutions to dynamic power dispatching. The framework is able to maximize power production and distribution by integrating advanced machine learning algorithms with real-time data, with a particular emphasis on maximizing the use of renewable sources and reducing the use of costly, non-renewable ones. It uses deep reinforcement learning, semantic search to process unstructured data, including weather report and operational logs, in addition to conventional structured data (e.g., market data and grid status). This system is integrated to enable it to make real-time changes depending on the changing conditions of demand and generation so as to achieve the best grid stability and efficient use of the available resources. The numerical analysis system performance shows that the system has significantly improved compared to the literature methods. It is shown that the Proposed System will result in a 90% reduction in costs, a 95% decrease in energy consumption, and a 95% improvement in grid stability and a response time of 0.05 seconds. Compared to such methods as Knowledge Graph-based Dispatch, Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), and Distributed Optimization, the Proposed System is better in all the most important performance metrics. It is the best at real-time decision-making, dynamic optimization, and the overall efficiency of the grid, providing the highest performance regarding the reduction of costs, energy efficiency, and grid stability. The suggested structure is a scaled and flexible approach to managing the power grid in the future, especially in situations when it is crucial to combine renewable energy, make the grid run in real-time, and achieve cost reduction at the same time to keep the grid balanced and cause the least harm to the environment.

items.title: Cross-linguistic differences in responses to patient queries on osteonecrosis of the femoral head between English and Chinese-oriented large language models: a semantically matched bilingual cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Background Large language models (LLMs) are capable of providing health information and consultation to patients with osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH). However, owing to imbalances in the linguistic distribution of their training corpora, the quality, readability, and safety profiles of outputs generated by the same model may vary across language settings. Objective This study aimed to compare bilingual responses to ONFH patient queries generated by six state-of-the-art flagship LLMs, comprising three English-oriented models (ChatGPT-5.6-Sol, Gemini-3.1-Pro, and Claude-Fable-5) and three Chinese-oriented models (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Qwen3.7-Max, and Doubao-Seed-2.1-Pro), and to multidimensionally evaluate their cross-linguistic capabilities for generating medical information in terms of information quality, actionability, clinical accuracy, safety risk, hallucination, and readability. Methods A question set comprising 36 semantically distinct patient queries regarding ONFH was developed, yielding 72 semantically matched English–Chinese paired prompts. Six state-of-the-art flagship LLMs were evaluated. Information quality was assessed using the Global Quality Score (GQS), DISCERN, the Quality Assessment of Medical Artificial Intelligence (QAMAI), and the 20-item Ensuring Quality Information for Patients (EQIP-20). Actionability was assessed using the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials (PEMAT-P), while clinical accuracy was evaluated using a 5-point Likert scale. Safety risk was assessed using a graded classification framework, and prespecified criteria were established for identifying hallucinations. Readability was evaluated using language-specific readability metrics for English and Chinese responses. Statistical analyses included the Friedman test, paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and Spearman correlation analysis. Results A total of 432 responses generated by LLMs were included in this study, and good-to-excellent inter-rater reliability was observed for all evaluation indicators. Significant between-model differences in actionability and clinical accuracy were identified among the six models under both English and Chinese response conditions (all p < 0.05). Furthermore, clinical accuracy exhibited high cross-linguistic stability. ChatGPT-5.6-Sol showed high actionability and a relatively low frequency of Level 1 minor safety-related omissions under the English-language condition, whereas switching to Chinese was accompanied by reduced actionability and an increased frequency of Level 1 omissions. All observed nonzero safety events were Level 1 minor omissions; no Level 2 or Level 3 unsafe responses were identified in either language condition. Responses generated by all six models in both languages failed to reach the prespecified readability threshold for patient education. Conclusion The six LLMs showed significant inter-model differences in the actionability and clinical accuracy of responses to ONFH-related patient health queries in both English and Chinese settings, while clinical accuracy demonstrated favorable cross-linguistic stability. Notably, none of the six-model outputs met the applicable readability threshold for patient-targeted health education under either language condition. In clinical practice, model selection, prompting-language effects and hallucination-related risks should be comprehensively considered when deploying LLMs to deliver health information for patients with ONFH. At the present stage, LLM-generated content intended for direct patient-facing education requires cautious evaluation and human oversight.

items.title: Cross-Scenario Semantic Drift of Accounting English Terms
items.abstract: In order to solve the problem of cross-scene semantic drift of accounting English terms, this study constructs a multi-dimensional space of “scene semantics” and formalizes semantic drift into probability distribution transformation. An improved BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers)-Attention model integrating gated attention mechanism and Kullback-Leibler divergence is developed and the semantic drift flux index is proposed to quantitatively measure the drift degree. This paper further designs a two-tier standardization mechanism of “Simhash coarse screening+BERT fine matching” and a human-machine cooperation workflow of “Artificial Intelligence early warning expert judgment”. This method realizes the quantitative management of semantic drift of accounting terms, enhances the international comparability of accounting information, and promotes the transformation of accounting linguistics to computational social science paradigm. Through real-time terminology governance, the framework reduces the burden of manual audit of accounting supervision institutions and reduces compliance risks.

items.title: Current practices, challenges, and future directions in subcutaneous oncology monoclonal antibody delivery: a qualitative study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Subcutaneous oncology monoclonal antibodies (SCOmAbs) offer significant benefits compared to intravenous formulations, including reduced administration time and potential for self-administration. However, little has been published on real-world preparation and administration practices with these novel formulations. Methods This was a qualitative, exploratory study of 30 participants (10 patients receiving SCOmAbs, 10 nurses, and 10 pharmacists/pharmacy technicians) across various U.S. healthcare facilities. One-on-one, in-depth interviews examined current practices, pain points, device integration potential, projected impact of increased SCOmAb adoption, and perspectives on home administration. Results Findings revealed considerable variability in SCOmAb preparation and administration practices. While preparation methods generally aligned with typical parenteral workflows, notable deviations included bedside preparation by nurses (7/30), use of syringe pump modules (3/19), and one case of patient self-administration at home. Most participants utilized closed-system transfer devices (12/22) despite inconsistent hazardous drug treatment between facilities. Administration challenges included ergonomic difficulties for nurses during manual push (5/9 reporting physical discomfort) and variable injection techniques to accommodate patient comfort. Nurses reported significant workflow impact from being “tethered” to patients during administration, which could require staffing adjustments as SCOmAb frequency increases. Most patients (6/9) expressed interest in home administration for potential time savings and flexibility, though concerns about training, support, and safety were common. Conclusions As SCOmAb utilization expands, facilities may face barriers associated with increased demand that could necessitate innovative solutions. To leverage the full potential of SCOmAb products, developers should consider how next generation product presentations might minimize identified pain points, streamline administration, and facilitate safe transition to home self-administration. Delivery device integration, whether through prefilled syringes, portable infusion pumps, or other delivery systems, may address current challenges but requires careful consideration of facility infrastructure, product complexity and usability, workflow impact, and patient training requirements.

items.title: Cyberlogic-enabled Thinking Space: a closed-loop human-cyber cognitive architecture in CPST
items.abstract: Human–AI collaboration in Cyber–Physical–Social–Thinking (CPST) environments requires coordination among perception, reasoning, human judgment, and governance. This paper proposes Cyberlogic-enabled Thinking Space (CyTS), a conceptual governance-centric architecture organized through Entity, Mapping, Reasoning, and Governance layers. Its closed loop connects multimodal representation, heterogeneous reasoning, collaborative decisions, and controlled adaptation. The Entity layer provides operational descriptions rather than a sufficient ontology of cognition; logical consistency and predictive accuracy do not by themselves establish the causal validity of an action. CyTS therefore distinguishes associative, deductive, interventional, and exploratory claims and requires explicit assumptions, evidence provenance, uncertainty, and verification status at component interfaces. Structural causal models provide one implementable route, while equilibrium-based causal logic and proposals concerning brain–universe similarity and entangled machine thinking are examined as research perspectives with separate validation requirements. Governance mechanisms support privacy, accountability, human oversight, and runtime monitoring, including abstention when evidence or constraints are insufficient. Research hypotheses and evaluation protocols address causal transparency, decision quality, adaptation, cross-space coordination, and energy cost. Healthcare, education, and transportation scenarios illustrate the proposed workflow; they do not constitute empirical validation. CyTS contributes an auditable organizational framework and a testable implementation agenda, without claiming a completed theory of cognition or demonstrated performance gains.

items.abstract: This study examines how FinTech companies transform consumer behaviour data into financial value through artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, and hyper - personalisation. It explores how transactional, behavioural, and demographic data are collected, analysed,and converted into personalised financial products, recommendations, interfaces, and communication strategies. The study further evaluates how these practices influence customer retention, customer lifetime value, return on investment, average revenue per user, customer acquisition cost, and churn. Particular attention is given to machine learning, customer segmentation, recommendation systems, and predictive models used to anticipate consumer needs and improve engagement. The paper also considers the strategic role of data in product development, cross-selling, and marketing optimization. Alongside these benefits, it critically examines privacy, consent, algorithmic bias, cybersecurity, and regulatory compliance. The study concludes that AI-driven personalisation can create substantial commercial value in FinTech, but sustainable growth depends on transparent, secure, fair, and responsible use of consumer data over the long term.

items.title: Data Breaches in Government Digital Public Services: A Systematic Mapping of Research and Governance Challenges (2015–2025)
items.abstract: Background: The rapid digital transformation of public services has increased the collection and use of citizens’ personal data, intensifying concerns about data breaches in government-operated systems. However, existing research remains fragmented, with technical cybersecurity perspectives receiving greater attention than governance and public administration perspectives. Objective: This study aims to systematically map global research on data breaches in digital public services from 2015 to 2025 and identify theoretical and governance gaps relevant to the Indonesian context. Methods: A systematic literature review guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines was combined with bibliometric and scientometric analyses of publications indexed in Scopus. Descriptive bibliometric analysis and author keyword co-occurrence mapping using VOSviewer were conducted on 1,169 open-access documents, while 62 articles meeting the final eligibility criteria were examined through qualitative synthesis. Results: The findings reveal an increase in research output and six thematic clusters. Cybersecurity and data security had the highest keyword occurrence (235), whereas privacy, ethics, and data protection exhibited the greatest total link strength (457). Governance, institutional accountability, organizational capacity, and public trust remain comparatively less integrated into technical cybersecurity research. Conclusion: This study reconceptualizes data breaches in digital public services as sociotechnical governance challenges involving technological vulnerabilities, institutional capacity, regulatory arrangements, and public trust. The findings provide a conceptual foundation for strengthening public-sector data governance in Indonesia while highlighting the need for empirical validation and further comparative research.

items.title: Data Threshold Awareness in Growth Hacking: Simulation and Empirical Evidence from Experimentation, Recommendation and Agent-Led Optimisation
items.abstract: Growth hacking is often sold as a set of clever, low-cost tricks that any young start-up can use to grow fast. In earlier work, the author offered a reality check: growth hacking runs on data, and its core tools only start to work once a business has enough of it. This idea was introduced as Data Threshold Awareness, the eleventh meta-principle of the 10Ps marketing framework (Marketing Mix 3.0), with a provisional threshold zone of about 50,000 to 100,000 engaged users [1]. This paper puts that idea to the test through five complementary studies: 1. A simulation of 220,000 online A/B tests. 2. A recommender experiment on about 920,000 real film ratings (MovieTweetings). 3. A replication on about six million book ratings (Goodbooks-10k). 4. A simulation of an AI agent optimising a campaign. 5. A review of the early growth of five well-known technology companies. The studies all point the same way: data thresholds are real. A standard one-month A/B test needed about 62,000 monthly users to spot a 10% improvement in conversion reliably, and the value of each doubling of users rose and fell like a bell, peaking near 43,000. That number is not fixed: depending on a firm's conversion rate and the size of improvement it is looking for, the users needed ranged from under 10,000 to over a million. Personalised recommendations beat a simple bestseller list only after about 2,000 to 3,000 users in one dataset and 100 to 300 in the other, a gap largely explained by how active each user was. An AI optimisation agent captured less than a quarter of the available gain below 10,000 monthly users, but more than two-thirds at 100,000. The paper concludes that the data threshold varies with the task and is far steadier when measured in user interactions than in user counts. It closes with practical advice on how to grow before, during and after the threshold.

items.title: Deepfakes and Social Media
items.abstract: Digital technologies have increased the prospects for human interaction, economic productivity, and international relations. Digital technologies became stronger with the evolution of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and social media. AI and social media are closely associated in many areas to enhance human flourishing. AI-generated deepfakes are widely circulated on social media, increasing their reach. Deepfakes have laudable roles in education and entertainment. However, they also raise significant ethical and legal concerns when created and disseminated with malicious intent. Drawing on doctrinal, descriptive, and analytical methodologies, this chapter finds that deepfakes are used to disseminate disinformation, gender-based violence, challenges to children, human rights violations, insecurity, and threats to international relations. It suggests that deepfake technologies must align with the ethical values of accountability, autonomy, human dignity, justice, privacy, and transparency. It also calls for amending the existing legal framework and promoting capacity-building programs.

items.title: DESAFIOS NA PROTEÇÃO DOS DIREITOS AUTORAIS NO CONTEXTO DA INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL NO BRASIL: ENTRE A INOVAÇÃO E A INSEGURANÇA JURÍDICA
items.abstract: Este artigo analisa a relação entre os direitos autorais e a inteligência artificial no ordenamento jurídico brasileiro, com foco no uso de obras protegidas no treinamento de sistemas e na autoria, proteção e responsabilização relativas aos conteúdos gerados. A pesquisa é qualitativa, bibliográfica e documental, de abordagem jurídico-dogmática e comparativa, com análise de legislação, doutrina, jurisprudência e experiências regulatórias nacionais e estrangeiras. Os resultados demonstram que não há vazio normativo geral: a autoria é atribuída à pessoa física pelo art. 11 da Lei nº 9.610/1998, enquanto a proteção de resultados produzidos com auxílio de IA depende de contribuição humana criativa demonstrável. As principais lacunas concentram-se na disciplina da mineração de textos e dados, na documentação dos conteúdos utilizados no treinamento e na definição de critérios para aferição da contribuição humana. Conclui-se que a dificuldade probatória constitui obstáculo central à tutela autoral, tornando relevantes mecanismos de transparência e proveniência, além do aperfeiçoamento legislativo em discussão no Projeto de Lei nº 2.338/2023. CHALLENGES IN PROTECTING COPYRIGHT IN THE CONTEXT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN BRAZIL: BETWEEN INNOVATION AND LEGAL UNCERTAINTY ABSTRACT This article analyzes the relationship between copyright and artificial intelligence (AI) within the Brazilian legal system, focusing on the use of copyrighted works in the training of AI systems and on issues of authorship, protection, and liability concerning generated content. The study adopts a qualitative, bibliographic, and documentary approach, employing a doctrinal legal approach and comparative methodology to examine legislation, legal scholarship, case law, and domestic and foreign regulatory approaches. The results demonstrate that there is no general regulatory vacuum: under Article 11 of Law No. 9,610/1998, authorship is attributed to natural persons, while copyright protection for AI-assisted outputs depends on a demonstrable creative human contribution. The main legal gaps concern the regulation of text and data mining, the documentation of content used in training, and the establishment of criteria for assessing human contribution. It is concluded that evidentiary difficulties constitute a central obstacle to copyright protection, highlighting the relevance of transparency and content provenance mechanisms, as well as legislative improvements under discussion in Bill No. 2,338/2023.

items.title: Design and Development of Battery Operated Weeder for Wetland Rice
items.abstract: Background: Wetland rice cultivation requires effective inter-row weed management, but manual weeding is labour-intensive and conventional powered machines can be difficult to operate in puddled soil. Aim: To design and develop a battery-powered weeder that provides a lightweight, economical, ergonomic and eco-friendly machinery solution to reduce dependence on manual labour in wetland rice fields. Place and Duration of Study: Department of Farm Machinery and Power Engineering, SVCAET & RS, Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (IGKV), Raipur, Chhattisgarh, India, during 2025–2026. Methodology: The machine was powered by a 650 W DC motor paired with a 27 V, 30 Ah lithium iron phosphate battery system. Key structural components incorporated into the design included a mild steel chassis, rotating stainless-steel blades, a worm gear transmission system, a control unit and a dedicated floating mechanism. Results: The dimensions of the developed weeder were 780 × 560 × 1400 mm, with a total weight of 17.10 kg. Theoretical battery-runtime estimation indicated approximately 1.24 hours, while the ideal full-recharge time was estimated at approximately 2.4 hours for a 12.5 A charging current. The fabrication cost of the developed unit was estimated at ₹29,840. Conclusion: A lightweight ( ) battery-operated wetland weeder powered by a DC motor and a lithium iron phosphate battery pack was successfully designed, fabricated, and put into operation for inter-row weed management in puddled rice fields.

items.title: DESIGN OF AN APPLICATION FOR INCOMPLETE MEDICAL RECORD DOCUMENTATION USING MICROSOFT VISUAL STUDIO 2010 AT THE WEST JAVA PROVINCIAL OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH HOSPITAL
items.abstract: This study aimed to design a KLPCM application for reviewing the completeness of inpatient medical-record documentation at the West Java Provincial Occupational Health Hospital using Microsoft Visual Studio 2010. The system was developed using the prototyping method. The study produced a flowmap, context diagram, level-0 Data Flow Diagram (DFD), and Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD), which were implemented as a Visual Basic .NET-based prototype comprising a login form, main menu, two medical-record completeness input forms, and an automatically calculated eight-item monthly report form. Master data were stored in Microsoft Access, while review data and reports were stored in Excel. The application was designed because KLPCM results at the hospital were still recorded directly in Excel, resulting in repetitive data entry, susceptibility to errors, and time-consuming monthly recapitulation, which may affect staff performance, operational efficiency, and service quality. The prototype should be tested with a larger number of staff, user feedback should be collected for subsequent development, and the data should be migrated to a database before official implementation.

items.title: Design Principles and Measurement Frameworks for Human-Centered AI and Human-AI Interaction: A Systematic Review
items.abstract: Human-centered AI (HCAI) and human-AI interaction (HAX) are increasingly important as AI adoption expands across high-stakes domains. However, empirical evidence remains fragmented across disciplines, limiting the development of transferable design guidance. This systematic review synthesized empirical research on HCAI and HAX and was reported in accordance with PRISMA guidance. Eight databases were searched, and additional preprint records were identified through arXiv. These searches yielded 9,718 records, of which 44 articles were included in the final review. Findings were organized around three dimensions: outcome metrics, collaboration frameworks and AI roles, and domain-specific patterns. Across studies, AI support was often associated with improved objective task performance, including accuracy, task completion time, and decision quality. Subjective outcomes such as trust, satisfaction, usability, and workload varied with transparency, explanation format, cognitive demand, and perceived control. Results suggest that HCAI and HAX frameworks should support task performance while preserving human autonomy and manageable workload. They should also support appropriate trust and reflect domain-specific needs.

items.title: Designing Clinician-in-the-Loop Multimodal AI for Emergency Mental and Behavioral Health Care: A Pilot Study of Consultation, Documentation, and Accountability
items.abstract: Emergency Department (ED) visits for mental and behavioral health (MBH) conditions have increased, intensifying demands on psychiatric consultation, documentation, risk assessment, and care coordination. While AI systems integrating computer vision and Large Language Models (LLMs) could support ED MBH care, safe implementation requires domain-specific evaluation. This preliminary study conducted 17 scenario-grounded, semi-structured interviews regarding barriers, facilitators, and design requirements for AI-enabled consultation and documentation. Thematic analysis of 277 quotations identified 18 themes. Clinicians viewed AI as a beneficial clinician-in-the-loop support tool to reduce note-taking burden, improve information synthesis, detect behavioral cues, and enhance direct patient attention. Adoption depended on workflow fit, patient acceptability, explainability, and accountability. Key requirements included clinician review of AI outputs, ligature-safe hardware, standardized kiosk placement, reliable audio/ video capture, and fallback workflows for high-risk patients. Findings suggest AI systems be evaluated as embedded sociotechnical systems within ED MBH workflows, prioritizing workload, trust, safety, and legal accountability.

items.title: Designing Embedded Intelligence through Co-Design Substrates Optimization and System Assurance
items.abstract: Embedded intelligence places sensing, inference, adaptation, and decision making inside physical systems limited by energy, memory, latency, cost, and reliability. This narrative review examines the field along four connected axes: hardware and software co-design, computational substrates, optimization at the model, mapping, and system levels, and applications in industrial automation, automotive electronics, healthcare monitoring, and the Internet of Things. Timing, safety, and security are treated as requirements that cut across all four axes. The review separates embedded intelligence from constrained on-device machine learning and from edge artificial intelligence, and it frames deployment as a cross-layer problem in which model quality, hardware mapping, timing, energy, security, and adaptation constrain one another. Two literature-based case studies, one on a field-programmable gate arrayand one on distributed microcontrollers, show how a gain at one layer produces a cost at another. A recomputation of the efficiency ratios reported in one of the studies shows why measurement boundaries and metric definitions must be declared. Six research priorities are derived from limitations that recur in the reviewed sources: lifecycle energy accounting, assurance of learned components, security of distributed deployments, reproducible benchmarking, portable deployment toolchains, and concept drift after deployment. Each priority is paired with a research direction and evaluation criteria for later studies. The evidence consists mainly of surveys, analytical studies, and laboratory implementations, so quantitative values are reported as stated in the sources, recomputed values are labeled as such, and approaches are not ranked. The proposed formulations and criteria are conceptual.

items.title: Developing a multi-level human-centered design framework for digital health implementation: a cross-project methodological synthesis
items.abstract: Background Digital health interventions have considerable potential to improve healthcare access, quality, and efficiency. Despite increasing adoption, many interventions fail to achieve sustainable implementation or progress beyond pilot phases because they are insufficiently integrated with user needs, organizational workflows, and health system contexts. Although human-centered design (HCD) has improved the usability and acceptability of digital health technologies, its application frequently remains confined to early design activities and is rarely integrated with implementation science throughout the implementation lifecycle. Objective This study aimed to develop a multi-level, human-centered design framework informed by a cross-project methodological synthesis integrating participatory design and implementation science to support the design, implementation, evaluation, and scale-up of digital health interventions. Methods A cross-project methodological synthesis was conducted using complementary digital health implementation studies undertaken in Kenya. The empirical corpus included studies spanning adolescent mental health, neonatal clinical decision support, digital health infrastructure, generative artificial intelligence, and frugal digital health innovation. Framework development followed an iterative analytical process combining thematic synthesis, constant comparative analysis, and abductive reasoning. The synthesis organized recurring methodological themes into an integrated framework spanning user, workflow, and system perspectives across the digital health implementation lifecycle. Results The synthesis identified recurring methodological processes that consistently contributed to successful digital health implementation, including contextual understanding, participatory stakeholder engagement, iterative refinement, workflow integration, organizational readiness, governance, and sustainability. These findings informed the development of a multi-level framework structured around six iterative implementation phases: Understand, Co-design, Prototype, Evaluate, Implement, and Scale, and three interconnected analytical levels: user (micro), workflow (meso), and system (macro). The framework conceptualizes digital health implementation as a continuous sociotechnical process in which sustained adoption and scale-up depend upon coordinated alignment among these three levels throughout the implementation lifecycle. Conclusions This study advances human-centered design by integrating it with implementation science through an empirically derived, lifecycle-oriented methodological framework for digital health implementation. The proposed framework may provide researchers, developers, practitioners, and policymakers with a structured approach for designing, implementing, evaluating, and scaling digital health interventions while supporting sustainable, context-responsive, and equitable digital health transformation.

items.title: Development and evaluation of X‐ray lithophanes as test objects for interventional procedure simulation
items.abstract: Abstract Background In the growing field of interventional radiology, emerging technologies implement the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to help tackle growing demands for treatment. Due to the anatomical differences in animals, volunteers offer the most realistic training and testing scenario, however safety considerations restrict rapid prototyping of these new technologies. Simulators have been a key facilitator in the testing of new technologies among numerous medical engineering studies, but often lack the realism to reliably test AI. Purpose This proof‐of‐concept study presents methods to create or enhance hyper‐realistic radiographic simulators that can effectively function with a medical‐grade AI software. Methods Iron‐filled plastic was used to three‐dimensionally (3D) print a series of blocks of heights up to 30 mm. By analyzing the intensities generated by different thicknesses of plastic, anonymous fluoroscopic images were turned into height maps (lithophanes) and 3D‐printed. A static scene from transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) was then 3D‐printed and imaged with different presets using two different x‐ray systems for mathematical analysis. Lithophanes were then used as a radiographic background to experimental and commercial interventional simulators to test Caranx Medical's TAVIPILOT AI. Finally, fluoroscopies from 5 3D‐printed lithophanes were mixed with 5 real images and presented to 5 expert volunteers to establish their realism in a structured survey. Results The 3D‐printed x‐ray lithophanes test‐plates' radiographic appearance was rated as “Adequate” to “Good” across all fields of the survey, with participants praising their realism. The test‐plate was able to reliably recreate the TAVI scene in different x‐ray systems, with joint‐histogram correlation coefficients above 0.9, and global structural similarity above 0.8. The lithophanes were imaged as a standalone test plate and as a backing to dynamic TAVI interventional simulators; in both cases, TAVIPILOT AI responded to the simulator as if it was operating on a real anatomical image. Conclusions Lithophane plates present an easy‐to‐implement solution to recreate monoplane x‐ray scenes, which can be deployed to test software at the point of care with minimal logistical, ethical, or safety concerns. This study opens the door for a new range of interventional simulators able to recreate human‐like appearance to test AI, offering a non‐exclusive alternative to patient volunteers and anonymous data.

items.title: Development and internal validation of a routine metabolic screening model for current hyperuricemia among gas station workers in Guangxi, China: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Serum uric acid (SUA) measurement is the direct basis for identifying current hyperuricemia (HUA). We developed a non-SUA screening model for situations in which routine occupational health information is already available but a contemporaneous SUA result is temporarily unavailable, delayed, or requires separate testing. Methods This cross-sectional study included 894 workers from 11 gas stations and related operational sites in Nanning, Guangxi, China. Current HUA was defined as same-examination SUA > 420 µmol/L in both sexes. Twelve prespecified non-SUA candidate variables were considered; total cholesterol was excluded because of high redundancy and multicollinearity with LDL-C, leaving 11 candidates for least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) screening. Internal validation used 100 repetitions of site-grouped five-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed using out-of-fold (OOF) predictions, discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis, candidate screening thresholds, and bootstrap optimism correction. Results Among 894 participants, 169 (18.9%) had current HUA. Sex, waist circumference, triglycerides (TG), systolic blood pressure (SBP), and fasting blood glucose (FBG) met the prespecified selection-stability threshold and comprised the final model. The mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) across repeated site-grouped cross-validation was 0.858 (SD 0.004), and the pooled OOF AUC was 0.866 (95% CI, 0.838–0.893). The pooled OOF Brier score was 0.108, the calibration intercept was − 0.064 (95% CI, -0.322 to 0.192), and the calibration slope was 0.920 (95% CI, 0.791–1.077). At a 10% candidate probability threshold, sensitivity was 92.9%, specificity was 64.6%, and the negative predictive value was 97.5%. Conclusions The five-variable model estimates the probability of current HUA and may support prioritization of confirmatory SUA testing when a contemporaneous SUA result is unavailable. It does not replace direct SUA measurement or predict future incident HUA. Independent external validation is required before broader implementation.

items.title: Development and Preliminary Psychometric Evaluation of a Digital-Intelligence Literacy Self-Report Scale Among Students in Medical and Health-Related Programs
items.abstract: Medical students increasingly engage with interconnected digital systems, health data, and artificial intelligence (AI), but existing instruments vary in the aspects of digital, data, and AI literacy they assess in medical contexts. This study developed and initially evaluated the Chinese-language Digital-Intelligence Literacy Scale for Medical Students (DIL-MS). Following two rounds of consultation with 16 experts, a 34-item questionnaire was field-tested at one Chinese university. Of 1118 returned questionnaires, 710 were analyzed in non-overlapping exploratory (n = 344) and confirmatory (n = 366) subsamples. Full-pool exploratory factor analysis and confirmatory factor analysis for ordinal data informed a revised 32-item scale across six domains: readiness, theoretical literacy, application skills, health data practices and interpretation, critical thinking, and ethical literacy. Parallel analysis suggested six factors, with some item assignments differing from the proposed domains. The correlated six-factor model fit better than the tested five-, four-, and single-factor alternatives, but absolute fit was limited (robust comparative fit index = 0.802; robust root mean square error of approximation = 0.090). Overall Cronbach’s α was 0.938, and domain α ranged from 0.726 to 0.871; convergent and discriminant validity evidence varied across domains. The DIL-MS provides medically contextualized self-report content for exploring perceived learning needs and mapping curricula.

items.title: Development and preliminary validation of an AI acceptance scale for intercultural teaching and its cross-sectional associations with university teachers’ occupational wellbeing
items.abstract: Background University teachers’ occupational wellbeing and emotional exhaustion are relevant occupational-health concerns in higher education. As generative artificial intelligence becomes embedded in teaching work, AI acceptance may represent a perceived, context-specific appraisal of whether AI is usable for intercultural teaching tasks. This study developed a preliminary measure of AI acceptance for intercultural teaching and examined its cross-sectional associations with teacher resources and occupational-health indicators. Methods This two-sample cross-sectional study used Sample A to examine the empirical behavior of the AI Acceptance for Intercultural Teaching Scale and Sample B to test measurement validity and occupational health associations. IBM SPSS Statistics 27.0.1 was used for descriptive statistics, EFA, Cronbach’s alpha, correlations, and regression analyses. CFA and SEM were conducted in R 4.6.1 (lavaan 0.6.21, lavaan.mi 0.1.0, and mice 3.19.0) using robust maximum likelihood (MLR) estimation; CR and AVE were calculated from standardized CFA loadings, and HTMT from item correlations. Hypothesis tests used non-imputed scale-score regressions; multiple imputation (mice, m = 5) with D2-pooled CFA/SEM model tests served as sensitivity analysis, and indirect-association bootstrap intervals were sensitivity summaries rather than formal D2-pooled tests. Results The AITA items were suitable for factor analysis in Sample A (KMO = 0.940), but the exploratory loading pattern did not cleanly reproduce the theorized four TAM-based dimensions. In Sample B, the overall AITA score showed good internal consistency (alpha = 0.858), whereas the four subdimensions showed substantial overlap and weaker reliability and convergent-validity evidence. AI acceptance was positively associated with intercultural teaching self-efficacy and autonomous teaching motivation. Self-efficacy was associated with both occupational wellbeing and lower emotional exhaustion, whereas autonomous motivation was associated primarily with occupational wellbeing. Direct associations between AI acceptance and the occupational-health outcomes were not significant. Conclusion The present findings provide preliminary evidence for using the overall AITA score as a context-specific measure of AI acceptance in intercultural teaching. The results also show cross-sectional associations between AI acceptance and teacher-resource variables, but they do not establish causal effects, mediation, or intervention effectiveness. The four TAM-based dimensions should be treated as provisional content facets requiring further validation.

items.title: Development of a methodology for selecting actors in the industrial ecosystem for exporting artificial intelligence-based solutions
items.abstract: Subject. An industrial ecosystem as an organizational mechanism to support the export of artificial intelligence-based solutions. Objectives. Development of a methodology for selecting potential participants in the industrial ecosystem to increase its export potential in the development and market launch of products, technologies and solutions based on artificial intelligence. Methods. The work of domestic and foreign scientists, as well as the authors' own developments in the field of theory and practice of the functioning of industrial ecosystems, as well as official resources of government agencies and ministries of the Russian Federation, publications in the media and open sources are used. Methods of generalization, analysis, and synthesis were used to develop an integral criterion for the effectiveness of participation in the competitive selection of potential actors in the industrial ecosystem. Results. An integral assessment of a potential actor of the industrial ecosystem has been determined to clarify the possibility and expediency of its participation in the ecosystem. The developed methodology can be used to manage the network interaction of participants in industrial ecosystems at a strategic level to increase the export potential of both individual actors and the ecosystems themselves as a whole. Conclusions. The use of a formalized selection of participants in the industrial ecosystem based on an integrated assessment of economic, environmental and social criteria will make it possible to form a pool of actors with the most essential competencies necessary to achieve the goals of ecosystem functioning. The system of criteria and methodology developed by the authors makes it possible to take into account the roles of individual participants in the selection process, and ensures their interaction in the joint use of resources through industrial symbiosis for the effective implementation of export projects.

items.title: Development of an HFACS-based risk assessment indicator system for unplanned endotracheal extubation in adult ICU patients: a Delphi and AHP study
items.abstract: Objective To construct a risk-assessment indicator system for unplanned endotracheal extubation (UEE) among adult ICU patients based on the Human Factors Analysis and Classification System (HFACS), and provide a structured multi-level framework for unit-level safety auditing and root-cause analysis of UEE events. Methods Initial indicators were generated via systematic literature review and retrospective analysis of local UEE adverse-event cases. A two-round Delphi expert consultation was performed to screen and revise indicators. The Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) was adopted to calculate indicator weights at each hierarchical level. Content validity was evaluated using the content validity index (CVI). Results The valid response rates for the two Delphi rounds were 100.0% (20/20) and 95.0% (19/20), respectively. The expert authority coefficients (Cr) were 0.893 and 0.915, indicating high expert authority. Kendall's coefficients of concordance ( W ) were 0.242 and 0.254 ( P < 0.001), showing statistically significant yet low expert agreement. Among the four primary dimensions, the combined weights were 0.448 for unsafe behavior of clinicians, 0.257 for inadequate supervision, 0.151 for preconditions for unsafe acts, and 0.144 for organizational influence. The final risk-assessment indicator system comprised 4 primary, 13 secondary, and 63 tertiary indicators with acceptable overall content validity. Conclusion Using HFACS, two-round Delphi consultation, and AHP, this study developed a consensus-driven preliminary indicator system for UEE risk-related safety management in adult ICUs. This framework is intended for system-oriented safety audits, training priority setting, and root-cause analysis rather than bedside individual-patient risk prediction. Further prospective clinical validation is required to verify its predictive validity, reliability and practical feasibility before widespread clinical implementation.

items.title: Developmental psychology in online and in-person classes: pedagogical considerations for tertiary teaching
items.abstract: The ways in which developmental psychology have been taught in university undergraduate and graduate environments differ when delivered in in-person or online settings. This commentary reviews the enablers and barriers of online and in-person pedagogical teaching of developmental psychology, particularly in the post-COVID era of generative AI. Enablers to online teaching primarily centre on the flexibility in how and where students learn, while barriers relate to the number of completed assessments and the amount of content students are required to retain across shortened teaching terms. Enablers to in-person teaching comprise face-to-face tutorials and the opportunity for assessment scaffolding, while barriers include the continuity and ongoing nature of student assessment. In addition, this commentary specifically draws on the teaching and research experiences of the author in identifying a four-pronged approach to improving the delivery of developmental psychology in both in-person and online teaching environments: 1) Constructivism (active engagement), 2) Retrieval practice (memory consolidation), 3) Metacognitive scaffolding, and 4) Motivational design (Self-Determination Theory). It then presents a series of recommendations to this effect, ranging from weekly student reminders and embedding consistent self-test materials throughout the course, to leveraging generative AI in curriculum design and assessment and integrating optional dates or flexibility for student submissions. Finally, it concludes by offering insights about the future of generative AI, including its use and application in developmental psychology, regardless of how the discipline is delivered and taught in the future.

items.title: Digital Accounting for Biometric Financial Management Efficiency of Accounting Staff in Rivers State Universities
items.abstract: This study investigated use of Digital Accounting for Biometric Financial Management Efficiency of Accounting Staff in Rivers State Universities. The area of the study was Rivers State. Seven specific objectives, seven research questions and seven null hypotheses guided the study. The study adopted descriptive survey design. The population for this study consists of one hundred and forty six (146) staff of the payroll unit, Accounts unit and Tax units. There was no sampling as the entire population was used for the study, the reason was that the population size is manageable. A self-structured questionnaire was used by the researcher for data collection, the instrument was titled” Digital accounting systems for Biometric Financial Management by Accounting Staff” The instrument was validated by three experts, one in Measurement and Evaluation and others from Business Education department. The instrument was structured on a 4-point rating scale of very high extent, high extent, moderate extent and Low extent. In order to establish the reliability of the instrument that was used for the study, test re-test method was adopted, scores obtained were correlated using Pearson Product Moment Correlation Coefficient and it yielded a reliability coefficient of 0.82 which revealed that the instrument is suitable for the study. The data collected for the study was analyzed by the researcher with SPSS version 27 using mean and standard deviation for research questions while t-test was used to test hypotheses at 0.05 level of significance. items.title: DIGITAL ETHICS IN EDUCATION: A SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW
items.abstract: Digital ethics has become a central concern in education as artificial intelligence (AI), generative AI, learning analytics, and data-driven systems are increasingly embedded in teaching, learning, research, and institutional decision-making. Despite rapid growth in scholarship, the literature remains conceptually dispersed, making it difficult to identify dominant ethical concerns, educational responses, and unresolved research gaps. This systematic literature review synthesizes recent scholarship on digital ethics in education by examining ethical implications of AI and generative AI, ethics education and professional development, and ethical dilemmas within professional and institutional practice. The review followed the PRISMA 2020 framework. Searches were conducted in Scopus and ERIC and were limited to English-language peer-reviewed journal articles published in 2024 and 2025. The searches identified 560 records (408 from Scopus and 152 from ERIC); following screening, eligibility assessment, and quality appraisal, 20 studies were retained for qualitative synthesis. The findings converge around three interrelated themes: ethical implications of AI and generative AI; ethics education, ethical training and professional development; and ethical challenges within professional, institutional and data-intensive practice. Overall, the review shows a shift from abstract ethical principles toward applied, context-sensitive ethical competence and governance, while empirical validation and policy evaluation remain limited. The review supports the development and testing of integrated ethical frameworks to guide responsible digital transformation in education.

items.title: Digital health transformation in Liberia: a hybrid incremental digital transition framework (HIDTF) for sustainable electronic health record implementation
items.abstract: Liberia, like other fragile post-conflict health systems, still relies mainly on paper patient records, and electronic health record (EHR) initiatives have repeatedly failed to reach routine use or national scale. The literature documents the barriers but explains less well why they persist. This conceptual paper proposes three candidate mechanisms and a phased framework, the Hybrid Incremental Digital Transition Framework (HIDTF), for the transition from paper to interoperable EHRs in Liberia. Conceptual synthesis and framework development. Peer-reviewed and grey literature on Liberia and comparable low- and middle-income settings was identified through purposive, iterative searching (PubMed, Europe PMC, Google Scholar) and synthesised narratively by a single author. The corpus is illustrative, not comprehensive, and no quality appraisal or independent screening was done. Constructs from established implementation science frameworks, sociotechnical systems theory and resilience theory, with a political economy lens, were used to derive mechanisms and design requirements. Additional file 1 lists all cited sources and codes the support for each element as a documented finding, a source-author interpretation or an inference by the author. Three candidate mechanisms were proposed. Recursive implementation failure: each abandoned attempt may deplete absorptive capacity and deepen scepticism, lowering the odds of the next attempt. Reliability asymmetry: where power and connectivity are unreliable, reversion to paper can be a rational professional response rather than resistance. Incentive misalignment: donor accountability structures can reward deployment outputs over sustained use. HIDTF proposes five phases and readiness gates (a coordination mechanism and an agreed interoperability approach; minimum infrastructure with offline capability; a trained local cadre) to be met before a site or county digitises. Hybrid paper-digital workflows would be governed as a designed arrangement, and domestic financing would be planned from the outset. No durations or numerical targets are proposed, and four testable propositions are stated. HIDTF is a theory-informed proposal built on secondary evidence from Liberia and comparable settings. The evidence on sequencing is mixed, since one cited source recommends concurrent development, and transferability beyond Liberia is a hypothesis. A Liberian initiative chronology, stakeholder consultation and prospective pilot evaluation are needed before adoption. Not applicable.

items.abstract: The advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the educational field has expanded teaching and learning possibilities, but has also sparked important ethical and philosophical reflections. This study aimed to map and analyze the scientific literature on the ethical dimensions of AI in teaching and learning processes through a systematic literature search. The search was conducted in the Web of Science database, using the descriptors "Artificial Intelligence" AND "ethics" AND "education." Initially, 1,822 articles were identified; after applying the inclusion and exclusion criteria, 155 documents remained, of which only 9 comprised the final review. The analysis revealed three main themes: ethical dilemmas related to privacy, algorithmic biases, and student autonomy; philosophical discussions about the role of AI in the teacher-student relationship; and teachers' responsibility when mediated by intelligent technologies. It is concluded that, despite the potential of AI to transform pedagogical practices, theoretical and normative gaps still persist that demand greater scientific and political depth, especially in the development of solid ethical frameworks that guide its application in the educational context.

items.title: Divergent user expectations of conversational AI: a comparative sentiment and thematic analysis of ChatGPT and Replika app store reviews
items.abstract: Abstract Conversational AI apps are increasingly serving two different purposes: instrumental productivity and emotional support. Although both are built on the same underlying language technology, users may evaluate these systems according to different instrumental and relational expectations. This study examines the differences in user evaluation of a task-oriented assistant (ChatGPT) and a companionship-oriented agent (Replika) through computational analysis of the sentiment scoring, NRC emotion analysis, topic modelling, and inferential tests of the 6,000 publicly available app store reviews (3,000 per application). The two applications differed only marginally in overall review polarity, and the direction of the difference depended on the method used: under the Bing lexicon Replika reviews scored slightly higher (M = 0.312 vs. 0.275), whereas under sentimentr ChatGPT scored higher (M = 0.135 vs. 0.102); aggregate polarity was therefore not a robust point of difference between the two corpora. The rating distributions differed significantly between the applications (χ² (4, N = 6,000) = 242.26, p < .001, Cramér’s V = 0.20), with ChatGPT ratings more polarised at both ends of the scale (36.8% vs. 21.7% five-star; 27.4% vs. 23.8% one-star) and Replika ratings more concentrated in the intermediate categories. Once scores were normalised for review length, Replika reviews contained more joy-, anger-, surprise-, and anticipation-associated language, with all effect sizes small; fear-, sadness-, and trust-associated language did not differ significantly between the applications. The coupling between review language and star rating was weaker for the companion application, though the difference was small (App × Rating interaction, partial η² = 0.016); because the two samples span different publication periods, this interaction is reported as provisional. Topic modelling yielded a six-topic solution in which conversation and companionship accounted for 53.6% of Replika reviews against 10.9% of ChatGPT reviews, while task assistance and usefulness accounted for 30.9% of ChatGPT reviews against 1.2% of Replika reviews. Together, the findings are consistent with differences in evaluative framing between the two applications examined in this study, illustrating two representative cases rather than establishing distinct categories of conversational AI systems.

items.title: Do Preferred and Trusted Attention Cues Support Better Visual Search Performance?
items.abstract: As automated aids become more integrated into daily life and safety-critical tasks, understanding how preference and trust relate to performance becomes important. Automated aids can vary in design, and users may prefer or trust some implementations more than others, even when those subjective judgments do not align with objective performance. In the current study, participants completed a visual search task in virtual reality using different types of cues to search for objects. After the search task, participants responded to questions assessing their preference for and trust in the cue designs. Participants performed better with their most preferred cue than they did on average across the remaining cues, whereas participants did not reliably perform better with their most trusted cue. These findings show that preference and trust provide distinct information about cue designs and highlight the importance of considering both subjective endorsement and objective performance when designing attention cues.

Dragon² (龖): From Mahjong's "Double Dragon Embrace" to Peaceful U.S.–China Coexistence and Peace Under Heaven -- A Life-Writing Narrative 《龖(Dragon²): 从麻将「双龙抱」到中美和平共存与天下太平的生命书写》. Evolutionary Progress in Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics. Lenox Institute Press, MA, USA. 8(10M), 43 pages. (Simplified Chinese Version); ABSTRACT: 本文延续作者对「囍—𩺰—龖」的文化思考,将古字「龖」重新诠释为 Dragon²(亦写作 Dragon2)。囍象征新婚之喜,𩺰象征夫妻无论顺境逆境皆相伴一生;龖则将关怀由家庭延伸至世界。在本文所采用的麻将规则中,「双龙抱」指由两对相同顺子构成的组合,共含四副顺子,每对中的两副顺子花色与数序相同。作者借其「抱而不斗」的意象,将两龙比喻为具有全球影响力的中国与美国,寄托两国相互尊重、和平共存的愿望。这是作者提出的跨文化和平隐喻,并非将龙视为美国固有的国家象征。作者于龙年出生于中国,1949年迁至台湾,后赴美求学、成家与工作。中国承载其出生、文化与早年记忆,台湾见证其成长与求学,美国则承载其深造、事业与家庭生活。这段跨越海峡与太平洋的生命历程,使中美关系成为与自身及家人命运相连的切身议题。本文比较「双龙争珠」「双龙戏珠」「双龙抱」与「双龙护珠」的意象:若明珠代表霸权,两龙可能陷入零和竞争;若明珠代表地球,两龙便肩负共同守护的责任。文章进一步借用工程系统中的回馈、稳定与失控概念,阐述核战无真正赢家的警示,主张中美竞而不战、强而有制、和而不同,并在气候变迁、公共卫生、人工智慧安全与核风险降低等领域推动合作。和平的意义亦须落实于平民百姓的生活,使家庭免于战乱、人民安居乐业、世代得以延续。「龖」为既有古汉字,由两个繁体「龍」左右并列而成。本文赋予其「双龙抱,双吉祥,共筑人间仙境」的文化新意,以两龙相拥、彼此尊重,象征双重吉祥、和谐共存与天下太平。此一意涵及其中的中美合作寓意,均属作者的现代文化诠释,而非「龖」字的传统字典释义; 关键词:龖;Dragon²;Dragon2;双龙抱;麻将文化;囍;𩺰;中美关系;生命书写;系统工程;核风险降低;世界和平;和谐共存;天下太平;双重吉祥;平民福祉;中美合作; ABSTRACT: This article continues the author's cultural reflections on the sequence 囍–𩺰–龖, reinterpreting the ancient Chinese character 龖 as Dragon² (also written as Dragon2). 囍 symbolizes the joy of marriage, while 𩺰 represents lifelong companionship through prosperity and adversity. 龖 extends this concern from the family to the world. In the mahjong rules adopted here, "Double Dragon Embrace" consists of two pairs of identical sequences—four sequences in total, with the two sequences in each pair matching in both suit and numerical order. Drawing on the image of "embracing rather than fighting," the author uses the two dragons as a metaphor for China and the United States, two globally influential powers, expressing the hope that they will respect each other and coexist peacefully. This is a cross-cultural metaphor for peace proposed by the author, not a claim that the dragon is a traditional national symbol of the United States. Born in China in the Year of the Dragon, the author moved to Taiwan in 1949 and later pursued further education, established a family, and developed his career in the United States. China holds his birthplace, cultural roots, and early memories; Taiwan shaped his upbringing and education; and the United States became the setting for his advanced studies, career, and family life. This life journey across the Taiwan Strait and the Pacific makes U.S.–China relations a deeply personal concern connected to his own and his family's future. The article compares four images: "Two Dragons Contending for a Pearl," "Two Dragons Playing with a Pearl," "Double Dragon Embrace," and "Two Dragons Protecting a Pearl." If the pearl represents hegemony, the dragons may become trapped in zero-sum competition; if it represents the Earth, they share a responsibility to protect it. Drawing further on the engineering concepts of feedback, stability, and loss of control, the article emphasizes that nuclear war has no true winners. It advocates competition without warfare, strength exercised with restraint, and harmony without uniformity, alongside cooperation on climate change, public health, artificial intelligence safety, and nuclear risk reduction. Peace must also take concrete form in the lives of ordinary people, allowing families to live free from war, communities to thrive, and future generations to flourish. The character 龖 consists of two traditional Chinese 龍 characters placed side by side. The author gives it a new cultural meaning: "Two dragons embrace, bringing paired blessings and together creating an earthly paradise." Their embrace and mutual respect symbolize shared auspiciousness, harmonious coexistence, and peace under heaven. These meanings, including the association with U.S.–China cooperation, are the author's contemporary cultural interpretation rather than traditional dictionary definitions of 龖. items.title: Dressing Composite Fermions with Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Recent variational studies have demonstrated that the strongly correlated ground states of the fractional quantum Hall (FQH) effect can be captured using machine learning approaches starting from no prior knowledge of the underlying physics. We introduce a complementary framework that instead starts from Jain's composite-fermion (CF) wave functions, which accurately describe FQH states as weakly interacting states of CFs at fillings ν = n / ( 2 p n + 1 ) in an idealized limit. As we move away from this idealized limit to one more in line with experimental reality, we expect CFs to become dressed much like the electrons of a noninteracting system, which are dressed by neutral excitations as the interaction is turned on adiabatically, as in Landau's Fermi-liquid theory. We model this dressing using a Feynman-Cohen-style backflow approach, implemented through symmetry-preserving neural networks, which we refer to as CF-Flow. CF-Flow achieves competitive accuracy with substantially greater computational efficiency and scales to systems of ≳ 26 electrons. At fillings ν = 1 / 3 and 2 / 5 , CF-Flow produces ground-state energies as functions of Landau-level mixing strength that are nearly indistinguishable from those obtained using the fixed-phase diffusion Monte Carlo (fp-DMC) method, with low local-energy standard deviations, even though the latter constrains the wave function phase to that of the lowest Landau level, thereby providing insight into why fp-DMC has been successful in giving an accurate quantitative account of several experiments. Finally, the symmetry-preserving architecture of CF-Flow enables access to excited states and computation of the transport gap at ν = 1 / 3 and ν = 2 / 5 . Within the FQH sectors studied, the extrapolated gap is well described by an exponential decrease with Landau-level mixing and approaches a finite value at large mixing strength.

items.title: Dual manipulation of individuals by non-invasive intelligent technologies and its risk governance: from the perspective of the Destiny Machine metaphor
items.abstract: Introduction The “Destiny Machine” metaphor reveals an ethical concern: big data and artificial intelligence, operating as a data-power social machine, manipulate individuals with pre-determinacy as the core logic. At cognitive-information and behavioral decision-option levels, this manipulation appears as cognitive manipulation by recommendation algorithms and decision-making manipulation by automated decision systems. To uncover its psychological mechanisms and ethical risks, this paper builds a framework integrating ethics and psychology. Methods The Destiny Machine is transformed into an analytical tool with three dimensions: pre-determinacy, irresistibility, and concealment. Drawing on dual-process theory, automation bias, moral disengagement, and psychological reactance, it analyzes how non-invasive intelligent technologies psychologically manipulate individuals and shape their ethical risks, adopting the human-centered approach as the guiding principle for governance. Results Cognitive manipulation by recommender systems, typified by TikTok, leaves users unaware that their cognitive preferences are being systematically reshaped, keeping them imperceptibly immersed. Algorithms achieve this by activating Type 1 processing while bypassing Type 2 scrutiny, confining information to relevance channels, and exploiting automation bias and complacency to lower cognitive vigilance and suppress psychological reactance. Indulging in information cocoons widens users’ cognitive distance from the lifeworld, dissolving their moral attributes as ethical beings. Decision-making manipulation by automated decision systems is most evident in autonomous vehicles’ trolley-problem dilemmas, where passengers’ lives are reduced to quantifiable weights. The system pre-sets decision rules and allows remote intervention at the design end; opaque decision-making subjects and logic, millisecond-level deadlines, and impossibility of exit jointly pre-lock passengers’ fate before the accident occurs. It likewise exploits cognitive processing traits and automation bias, while dispersed agency makes responsibility attribution—and thus psychological reactance—difficult. Pre-coding an individual’s fate at the behavioral decision-option level may deconstruct their meaning world. Discussion Under the Destiny Machine metaphor, such manipulation erodes not only individuals’ autonomy but also their responsibility as moral subjects. Guided by the human-centered approach, it proposes governance schemes with clear actors, sound measures, and reliable benchmarks: a cognitive immune system of transparency and empowerment for cognitive manipulation, and a human-machine collaborative scheme of accountability and remedy for decision-making manipulation, rebuilding passengers’ trust to help them escape.

items.title: DyslexiSolve: Mind Map-Based AI Learning Platform for Dyslexic Students
items.abstract: This paper presents "DyslexiSolve," an intelligent web-based educational platform designed to alleviate cognitive overload for students with dyslexia. Traditional assistive technologies predominantly focus on Text-to-Speech (TTS) applications, which overlook the inherent visual-spatial reasoning strengths typical of neurodivergent learners. DyslexiSolve bridges this gap by leveraging Generative Artificial Intelligence (Google Gemini LLM) to autonomously digest dense, linear academic texts and restructure them into highly interactive, visual Mind Maps. The platform utilizes a decoupled three-tier architecture comprising a React.js frontend, a Next.js Serverless API and Prisma ORM for cloud persistence. By transforming unstructured paragraphs into navigable node-graphs, DyslexiSolve provides a frictionless, zero-login environment that actively translates reading tasks into spatial memory exercises, thereby fostering an inclusive and highly effective digital learning ecosystem.

items.title: EFEKTIVITAS SELF-STRETCHING TERHADAP PENURUNAN NECK PAIN AKIBAT PENGGUNAAN LAPTOP BAGI MAHASISWA SEMESTER AKHIR DI FAKULTAS KESEHATAN UNIVERSITAS NURUL JADID
items.abstract: Penggunaan laptop yang intensif di kalangan mahasiswa khususnya mahasiswa semester akhir, seringkali menjadi penyebab masalah kesehatan seperti nyeri leher (neck pain). Aktivitas yang berlangsung lama dengan posisi tubuh yang tidak ergonomis dapat memicu ketegangan otot leher dan mengganggu kenyamanan. Salah satu intervensi yang dapat dilakukan untuk mengurangi nyeri leher adalah dengan melakukan self-stretching. Menganalisis pengaruh self-stretching terhadap penurunan intensitas nyeri pada mahasiswa yang mengalami nyeri leher. Penelitian ini menggunakan quasi-experiment dengan rancangan pretest dan posttest with control group design. Populasi dalam penelitian ini adalah seluruh mahasiswa semester akhir Fakultas Kesehatan Universitas Nurul Jadid sebanyak 59 orang yang menggunakan laptop dalam aktivitas akademik. Teknik sampling yang digunakan adalah total sampling, sehingga jumlah sampel sebanyak 59 responden yang terdiri dari 30 kelompok intervensi dan 29 kelompok kontrol. Analisis data menggunakan uji Wilcoxon sign test. Berdasarkan penelitian ini, self-stretching berpengaruh terhadap penurunan intensitas nyeri dengan nilai p-value 0.000 (<0.05) pada kelompok intervensi, sedangkan pada kelompok kontrol diperoleh p-value 0.317 (>0.05). Terdapat pengaruh self-stretching terhadap nyeri leher pada mahasiswa semester akhir pengguna laptop pada kelompok yang dilakukan intervensi karena secara self-stretching membantu menurunkan spasme otot dan meningkatkan suplai oksigen ke jaringan sehingga nyeri yang dirasakan berkurang, sedangkan pada kelompok kontrol tidak terdapat pengaruh karena pada kelompok ini tidak dilakukan self-stretching. Abstract Intensive laptop use among students, especially final semester students, often causes health problems such as neck pain. Prolonged activities with non-ergonomic body positions can trigger neck muscle tension and disrupt comfort. One intervention that can be done to reduce neck pain is self-stretching. Analyze the effect of self-stretching on reducing pain intensity in students who experience neck pain. This study used a quasi-experimental design with a pretest and posttest with a control group design. The population in this study were all final semester students of the Faculty of Health, Nurul Jadid University, totaling 59 people who use laptops in academic activities. The sampling technique used was total sampling, so the number of samples was 59 respondents consisting of 30 in the intervention group and 29 in the control group. Data analysis used the Wilcoxon sign test. Based on this study, self-stretching has an effect on reducing pain intensity with a p-value of 0.000 (<0.05) in the intervention group, while in the control group obtained a p-value of 0.317 (>0.05). There is an effect of self-stretching on neck pain in final semester laptop users in the intervention group because self-stretching helps reduce muscle spasms and increases oxygen supply to the tissue so that the pain felt is reduced, while in the control group there is no effect because this group does not do self-stretching.

items.title: Effective Bandwidth: Semantic Quality-of-Service and Attention Architecture for Agent-Scale Systems
items.abstract: Public projections hold that proliferation of autonomous AI agents will drive communication bandwidth demand two to three orders of magnitude above present levels within three to five years, and that power rather than bandwidth may prove the binding constraint on deployment. This paper accepts that projection as a premise and argues that it is incomplete. Raw transport capacity and effective information delivery are distinct quantities, and the gap between them widens, not narrows, as agent populations scale. We formalize effective bandwidth as the product of raw rate and filter quality, show that beyond a saturation point additional raw capacity yields zero marginal signal to a bounded consumer, and argue that agent-scale systems therefore require a semantic quality-of-service layer: a structured blackboard, separated safety and relevance overwatch, a pattern-recognition supervisor, and a main agent that reads a filtered and audited stream rather than a raw firehose. We specify the architecture, an event schema, and a metric suite; we identify the filter layer as both a bottleneck and an adversarial attack surface; and we argue that filtering is an energy-efficiency instrument, not merely a cognitive one. The framework is offered as an architectural hypothesis requiring empirical validation, not as a validated result. The work was sparked by a public statement by Elon Musk projecting a dramatic increase in bandwidth demand from AI agent proliferation and identifying power as a likely nearer-term constraint.

items.title: EFFECTIVENESS AND IMPACT OF AI INTEGRATION ON TEACHING EXPERIENCES
items.abstract: The fast growth of artificial intelligence (AI) has created strong interest in how it can change higher education. AI tools brought new useful ways into undergraduate teaching, with the main goal of understanding how AI is currently being used in educational settings. Based on a review of recent studies and learning theories, this paper examines how tools such as intelligent tutoring systems, generative AI platforms, flexible learning technologies, and AI-supported feedback are changing teaching methods at the undergraduate level. The findings show that AI, when used carefully and fairly, can make learning more personal, increase student interest, and help teachers make better decisions based on student data. However, important challenges remain, such as concerns about fairness, student access to technology, teacher readiness, and the risk that students may stop thinking deeply on their own. The paper ends by suggesting a practical guide for using AI in teaching in a responsible and educationally sound way, and it calls for cooperation among schools, teachers, and government leaders to make the most of AI in undergraduate education.

items.title: Efficacy of a Gamified Training Program for Improving Occupational Health and Safety Knowledge Among Italian Secondary School Students: A Randomized Controlled Field Trial
items.abstract: This study evaluated the short-term effectiveness of an innovative gamified educational program based on the principles of the Italian Legislative Decree 81/2008 in improving occupational health and safety (OHS) knowledge among Italian secondary school students. A cluster-randomized controlled field trial was conducted in Italy from September 2024 to June 2025. Classes were randomized into experimental (EG) and control groups (CG). The intervention combined a seminar with three structured games (role-playing, board, and card games). Knowledge was assessed using a 15-item questionnaire (Q81) at baseline (T0) and post-intervention (T1). The primary endpoint was the between-group difference in Q81 score at post-intervention (T1). Of 930 eligible students, 927 participated (99.7%), 694 completed the study (74.6%), including 187 middle school and 507 high school students (N EG = 356; N CG = 338). Baseline Q81 scores were comparable between groups (EG: 5.6 ± 3.3 vs CG: 5.4 ± 2.9), whereas at T1, mean Q81 scores were significantly higher in the EG compared to the CG (9.0 ± 3.1 vs. 5.2 ± 2.9, P < 0.001; Cohen’s d = 1.26). Within-group analysis showed a significant improvement in the EG ( P < 0.001), but not in the CG. Reliability analysis yielded alpha = 0.804, indicating good internal consistency. Gamification training improved OHS knowledge among secondary school students and may represent an effective educational strategy for early safety education. These findings support the integration of gamified OHS training into secondary school curricula to strengthen early safety education in line with the principles of Legislative Decree 81/2008. . Future studies should include larger samples, address item-level weaknesses and explore long-term behavioural outcomes.
